name: West International
summary: The test field's parallel-runway airliner airport: 36L/18R and 36R/18L 1,310 m apart, a parallel taxiway inside each, stubs and exits to both, and a midfield terminal on each side of the field between them, with 747 and 737 gates and remote stands.
frame: Metres, in the frame of runway 36L/18R (airfield testfield_west_36l): `along` from its middle toward its far end, the NORTH end (18R's threshold; a 0-degree runway's threshold is its south end); `across` from its centreline, positive to the EAST, toward runway 36R/18L (airfield testfield_west_36r), which runs along the frame 1,310 m east: its places are `testfield_west_36r.centreline` and `testfield_west_36r.edge` across, and its ends `testfield_west_36r.threshold` and `.far_end` along. Heights are from the runway's level.

sources.standards: Cape International's, FAA AC 150/5300-13B change 1 for the 747-400 (ADG V, TDG 5, AAC D): see world/airbases/cape_international.
sources.layout: A midfield layout between parallel runways, on the pattern of Atlanta's (KATL) concourses between its runway pairs, cut to the two terminals this map needs. Each runway has a parallel taxiway on its inner side at 400 ft (Cape's `runway_to_taxiway`), stubs at both ends and the middle with hold bars, one 30-degree high-speed exit in each direction of landing, and an apron taxilane 250 ft further in (`taxiway_to_taxilane`, rounded as Cape's). The terminals face their own runway's taxilane across a nose-in apron, back to back across the 560 m of ground between them.
sources.spacing: 1,310 m centreline to centreline: FAA JO 7110.65 5-9-7, simultaneous independent ILS approaches to parallel runways 4,300 ft apart.
sources.remote: Six remote power-out stands for 747s, three each end of the west terminal: laid as Cape International's are, off the base's own runway's taxilane. Three on the east side, facing 36R's taxilane, would not hold a 747: the plan points a remote stand's nose away from the base's own runway, so the east side's were a hull's length short.
sources.cross: Two taxiways across the field between the parallel taxiways, 1,000 m either side of the middle, clear of the aprons: without them a 747 from a stand on 36L's side had no route to 36R's hold bars, and lined up from where it stood, across the grass.
